name: HYDRA
summary: A machine-learning kiosk prototype that assesses hydration from an eye scan, a urine reagent strip and a finger pulse sensor, then dispenses the water volume suggested by the result.
result: Combines eye-image features, urine specific gravity, heart rate and SpO₂ to assess hydration and dispense water.
keywords: hydration dehydration eye tear meniscus heart rate oxygen saturation sensor multimodal machine learning health prototype kiosk urine reagent strip specific gravity water dispenser touchscreen students computer vision multimodal sensor fusion yolo machine learning

blocks.text: HYDRA is a machine-learning prototype designed to assess hydration status and identify possible dehydration. It combines several inputs instead of relying on one signal: an enclosed eye-scan camera, a urine-strip camera and a finger pulse sensor. It then dispenses filtered water in an amount based on the hydration risk.

blocks.caption: Technology and methods
rows: U-Net isolates the tear-meniscus region in each eye image. Six parameters are extracted: area, mean thickness, maximum thickness, curvature, continuity and intensity.
YOLOv11 detects the urine reagent strip and its specific-gravity (SG) pad. Training images were annotated in CVAT.
A Support Vector Machine (SVM) combines the image-derived features with heart rate and SpO₂ to separate hydration categories.
MAX30102 optical sensor for heart rate and SpO₂. An enclosed eye-scan camera with uniform LED lighting, and a urine-strip camera with controlled lighting.
Touchscreen interface, filtered water reservoir, and a dispenser pump with its control system.

steps.label: Scan eyes
steps.detail: Enclosed camera with LED lighting captures the lower-eyelid tear meniscus

steps.label: Analyze urine
steps.detail: Internal camera reads a reagent strip for specific gravity, with YOLOv11 detecting the strip

steps.label: Measure pulse
steps.detail: Finger sensor (MAX30102) reads heart rate and SpO₂

steps.label: AI analysis
steps.detail: U-Net segmentation and an SVM classifier combine the data

steps.label: Dispense water
steps.detail: Touchless dispenser delivers the volume matched to hydration risk

items: Eye scan: an enclosed module with uniform LED illumination, similar to an ophthalmic device, captures the tear meniscus.
Segmentation: U-Net isolates the relevant region in each eye image.
Urine analysis: a discreet camera with controlled lighting reads the reagent strip for specific gravity (SG). YOLOv11 detects the strip and its specific-gravity pad in the image.
Physiological sensing: a MAX30102 optical sensor supplies heart rate and blood-oxygen saturation (SpO₂).
Classification: a Support Vector Machine analyses the extracted features and distinguishes hydration categories.
Hardware: touchscreen interface, water reservoir with filtration, and a dispenser pump with control system.

blocks.text: Six image-derived parameters describe the tear meniscus: area, mean thickness, maximum thickness, curvature, continuity and intensity.

items: Intended use: hydration awareness for students and general wellness. It is not a diagnostic device.

blocks.text: Next steps: collect a larger labelled dataset across lighting conditions and skin tones, report classification metrics for each input, and compare the combined model with each single input.
